I believe in the whole ball of you have a copy of the staff report that we've presented. Because that we are adopting are going to be The 2021 fire code, the 2021 international building code, the 2021 international field gas code, 2021 international mechanical code, 2021 international existing building code. Currently we are required by state statute to adopt codes as the state of Wyoming adopts them within six months. Obviously currently the state of Wyoming is working under the 2021 codes as red. We have had several public meetings and meetings with what we're titling the contractor city 2021 code adoption committee. that committee has met on November 7th. We met again on the 29th. And then we followed that up with a meeting, open house meeting at the Kiwanis Community House on December 1st. Through the meeting with the committee, there were a few items that stood out as, um, what I would term the bigger items, a bigger hitters that we needed to have discussion about. I will review those as we had that discussion. The first item that we needed to discuss was four plexes and the suppression of those. There is an ordinance currently in place within city ordinance that allows the installation. of a firewall or a two-hour firewall that would eliminate the requirement for the suppression system. That requirement for the suppression system is still in the codes that we're talking about adopting. The proposal is to remove that city ordinance and require the installation of fire suppression in those four plexes. The next item that was one of our large items was the existing building. I'm sorry, the energy code that we're going to adopt, the 2021 energy code has a number of items that are required that are pretty restrictive. docs.title: Word-for-word transcript — Work Session 10 28 22
docs.bodySnippet: [Transcript of the meeting video — Work Session 10 28 22] Context/Agenda: # Work Session: 10/28/22 Context/Agenda: thank you okay thank you so much since it is uh 12 o'clock according to the TV screens welcome to the October 28 2022 work session to receive information and recommendations from the affordable tax housing task force this meeting is open to the public however no public comment will be taken I've already spoken to our presenter today uh she is at the luxury of council that she says you can stop her at any time during her discussion and ask any questions throughout the meeting so we do not have to do q a at the very end and uh with that I will go ahead and let Brenda take the floor and do her introductions and follow the agenda accordingly thank you so much President Johnson members of the council thank you so much for your time today we are excited to present um our findings today my name is Brenda Berkel and I served as the chair of the affordable housing task force I have several members with me today including Keith zabka who is sitting to my right and he will be available for questions as well and served on the Innovations committee um so as you might recall uh resolution 3161 that formed us um set item seven charged us with uh projecting an Infuse future housing needs and conditions in inventory through 2030 analyzing and evaluating current policies and programs and initiatives and finally the third item was to recommend for the creation of new policies programs or initiatives and expansion of existing ones when we looked at the body of work that that encompassed our 15-member committee broke into three groups or committees that would attack each one of those deliverables and present them in a in the August report that was submitted last year as well as this final report the study committee began its work and pretty quickly it became apparent that the time and resources needed or necessary to conduct a full qualified housing study wasn't something that was going to be um doable without outside resources so what we did do is we had the assistance of the U.S Air Force Academy's Cadet Capstone program and we put in a grant we put in for a grant to be considered for their program and we were successful that program created a comprehensive analysis that included and it was included in your report my arms and push foreign good evening everyone I would like to call the September 26 meeting of the governing body to order Madam clerk would you take role Mr Roybal Councilman Segrave here Mr White president Dr. Aldrich president mayor Collins here Mr cook here Mr Esquibel here Mr Johnson president Mr Lamar president Dr Rooney president one member is absent mayor we do have a quorum he joined me in the Pledge of Allegiance please the United States of America and to the Republic for which it stands one nation under God indivisible with liberty and Trust all right I didn't know if anyone was here today to uh for the public hearing for the proposed trade of real property did anybody come here for that today all right that's great news because we had a small mistake in our date um and actually we'll have a announcement for that public hearing tonight and the actual public hearing will be held on October 10th so stay tuned for that I'm sure it'll be riveting next item please number four consent agenda all items listed with the designation of CA are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion there will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body cell request and support by two other members is received any item removed from the consent agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda all right is there anyone on the governing body like to remove an item from the consent agenda Mr Mayor Mr cook uh yes sir I would like to remove number 18. okay concur all right number 18 has been removed anyone else Mr Mayor I'd like to remove 24f from the consent agenda concur all right we'll remove 24f anyone else Dr. Rinne concur sure all right 17. anyone else in the governing body Mr white one more um I'd like to remove item 25A all right so we have four items to this point anyone else all right hearing none I would entertain a motion second moved by Mr Johnson seconded by Mr White all those in favor please signify by saying aye aye aye those opposed so the consent agenda is approved with numbers 18 24f 17 and 2580 removed next item please next item is number six ordinance emergency reading amending section 10.08.10 state law adopted of chapter 10.08 traffic laws adopted of title 10 vehicles and traffic of the municipal code of the city of Cheyenne Wyoming to update the incorporation of State motor vehicle statutes all right um just for the audience we have a situation where we found I think we'll probably get a staff report here but we found a loophole in our calls or now that we have a code enforcement officer if he sees anything that's obviously just obvious out in the field that is a zoning violation we'll start enforcement action on those process right now is a first notice which is then gives the person who's in violation 20 days to remedy that issue um and then if nothing is done in 20 days there's a final notice which is another 10 days and then it goes to the attorney's office to go to municipal court uh for prosecution um I would say right now just from speaking with our co-enforcement officer we're about most people are coming into compliance before we reach the end of that final notice so we aren't actually having to go as far to take anybody to court um so that's kind of how our process works right now we do work with the different property owners depending on timelines it's not always the strict 20 days we do work with them depending on what their what they're working on what they need to do to bring it into compliance and things like that so with this amendment some of the big changes in here that we'd be looking at is changing up the penalties so currently right now the only penalty we have is 100 a day while in violation I'm not sure exactly how strict we've been on that and if we've ever actually gotten to that point of charging 100 a day but that is in our current code for anybody in violation what we're looking at changing that to is just stating that you can be charged up to the state basically the maximum allowed by state statute so instead of the hundred dollars a day it could be 750 a day while you're in violation the two new tools that we're hoping council will agree with and ultimately approve with when this text amendment goes through is revocation or suspension of a permit or license or abatement of the violation so with revocation or suspension
